prompt: The popularity of fast food is increasing, especially among younger people. What are the cause for this trend? Is it a positive or negative development?
essay:
In recent years, people have been able to purchase a variety of food beyond country boundaries because of increasing globalisation. State-nations promote economic interdependence, and specifically, major fast food chain stores have spread worldwide and have served their product. Therefore, people, in particular the youth, frequently eat fast meals and some of them become obese or suffer from other lifestyle diseases. I assume this trend results mainly from the availability of such kinds of food, and this factor negatively affects our daily life.

Concerning the first point, fast food attracts particularly younger generations because of its price and taste. Fast food, such as hamburgers, potatoes, and nuggets are sold at an affordable price in various shops, grocery stores, and supermarkets. Additionally, they are tasty, so some people often eat these products with beverages. In Japan, a lot of students and young workers take out their breakfast or lunch from McDonald's because the company offers various set menus, hamburgers and appetisers with a cup of coffee or tea, ranging from 500 yen to 900 yen, and the stores are located in almost all prefectures. They choose fast meals as their daily meals to save money, and avoid waitingin along line to eat. In other words, the service which fast food chain serves meets modern public demands.

Regarding the second point, the spread of fast food changes makes the younger generation addicted to oil, sugar, and fat; this also leads to gaining weight, discourages them from exercising and having good concentration. Since their brain and bones are still  developing,  ingredients such as artificial additives exacerbate their health and decrease the levels of their concentration. In fact, statistics prove that children who have a healthy daily habit tend to bother less physical and mental health problems, and receive higher test scores at school than those who eat fast food on a daily basis. Despite some merits mentioned in the previous paragraph, people should realise that these kinds of cuisine contain ingredients worsening their physical health, and making a habit of eating these products may bring about negative outcomes in their academic performance as well.

To conclude, it is understandable that eating fast food becomes popular among kids, teenagers and adolescents in terms of price, convenience, and suiting their needs. On the other hand, this trend has a potential possibility of preventing them from keeping in good shape and achieving their goals , including getting a desirable test score.
